title: Two Signals, One Fast Generator: How rCM Distills Diffusion
summary: rCM combines continuous-time consistency with score-based distribution matching to preserve few-step speed while correcting detail errors and reducing diversity loss.
prerequisites: Vectors, gradients, and ordinary differential equations
Knowledge distillation from teacher to student
objectives: Explain how a noise schedule defines a diffusion trajectory.
Derive why continuous-time consistency uses a Jacobian-vector product.
Distinguish offline consistency training from on-policy score matching.
Explain how rCM balances detail quality and sample diversity.
Interpret the reported image and video results within their stated conditions.

claims.statement: The forward diffusion process can be reparameterized as x_t = alpha_t x_0 + sigma_t epsilon with standard Gaussian epsilon.
claims.conditions: For the paper’s continuous diffusion formulation with a predefined noise schedule.

claims.statement: A consistency model maps any point on a teacher PF-ODE trajectory to the trajectory’s clean endpoint and enforces the identity boundary at time zero.
claims.conditions: For trajectory points generated by the teacher probability-flow ODE.

claims.statement: Continuous-time consistency differentiates the student output along the teacher trajectory, producing a spatial Jacobian-vector product plus an explicit time derivative.
claims.conditions: In the limit of adjacent consistency times approaching one another under squared Euclidean distance.

claims.statement: The authors wrap teachers trained with other noise schedules into the TrigFlow schedule by matching signal-to-noise ratios, without retraining the teacher.
claims.conditions: When the reverse time mapping solving sigma/alpha = tan(t) exists and the parameterizations can be converted.

claims.statement: The large-scale implementation performs JVPs inside attention and layer boundaries so that FlashAttention-2, FSDP, and context parallelism remain usable.
claims.conditions: For the infrastructure described for large image and video transformer training.

claims.statement: Pure sCM exhibited fine-detail and temporal-consistency failures that the authors interpret as accumulated error amplified by JVP self-feedback at large diffusion times.
claims.conditions: In the reported text-to-image and text-to-video scaling investigation, especially under detail-sensitive prompts and video motion.

claims.statement: rCM minimizes L_rCM = L_sCM + lambda L_DMD, combining local continuous-time consistency with a score-distillation regularizer evaluated on student-generated samples.
claims.conditions: For the proposed rCM training procedure, with lambda controlling the relative DMD contribution.

claims.statement: The DMD component uses an auxiliary fake-score network as a proxy for the intractable score of the few-step student distribution.
claims.conditions: When optimizing reverse divergence on diffused samples generated by the student.

claims.statement: Student rollouts use a randomly chosen number of steps and nonincreasing stochastic times, while gradients from DMD pass only through the final denoising step.
claims.conditions: For the paper’s rCM rollout strategy with the number of steps sampled from 1 through N_max.

claims.statement: A 14B Cosmos-Predict2 rCM obtained a GenEval overall score of 0.83 at four function evaluations.
claims.conditions: At 1360 by 768 resolution on the paper’s GenEval evaluation.

claims.statement: A 14B Wan2.1 rCM obtained a VBench total score of 85.05 at two function evaluations and 8.3 frames per second.
claims.conditions: For 832 by 480 by 81 video, batch size one on one H100, including sampling and VAE decoding.

claims.statement: Increasing lambda in the reported Wan2.1 1.3B ablation improved quality but reduced diversity, while decreasing it produced the opposite tendency.
claims.conditions: For lambda in {1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001}, batch size 64, and 10,000 training iterations.

claims.statement: A distilled model exceeding a teacher on an aggregate benchmark does not establish that it is strictly superior in diversity or physical consistency.
claims.conditions: When interpreting the reported GenEval and VBench comparisons.

sections.title: The endpoint hidden inside a noisy state
sections.markdown:
A diffusion model begins with clean data $\bm{x}_0\sim p_{\text{data}}$ and progressively mixes it with Gaussian noise. At time $t$, the paper writes

$$\bm{x}_t=\alpha_t\bm{x}_0+\sigma_t\bm{\epsilon},\qquad \bm{\epsilon}\sim\mathcal{N}(\bm{0},\bm{I}).$$

Here $\bm{x}_0$ is a clean image or video latent, $\bm{x}_t$ is its noisy version, $\alpha_t$ is the retained signal scale, $\sigma_t$ is the noise scale, $\bm{\epsilon}$ is standard Gaussian noise, and $\bm{I}$ is the identity covariance. The corresponding probability-flow ODE supplies a deterministic velocity field whose trajectories share the diffusion process’s marginals.

The noise figure below isolates one geometric prerequisite. It draws seeded Gaussian vectors in $D$ dimensions and compares their measured norms with the RMS radius $\sigma\sqrt{D}$. Raising $\sigma$ lengthens vectors; raising $D$ makes their relative radii more concentrated. This helps explain why a diffusion time is not merely an image-opacity slider: it places data in a dimension-dependent noisy distribution. The display is illustrative, not a measurement from rCM, and its histogram does not represent learned image or video latents.

sections.title: Consistency as endpoint prediction
sections.markdown:
A consistency model learns $\bm{f}_\theta(\bm{x}_t,t)$, a function intended to return the same clean endpoint from every point on one teacher trajectory. The parameters are $\theta$, and the boundary condition

$$\bm{f}_\theta(\bm{x},0)\equiv\bm{x}$$

ensures that an already-clean state maps to itself. In practice, a skip connection and a learned network $\bm{F}_\theta$ enforce this boundary while retaining expressive power.

Discrete consistency training compares predictions at $t$ and $t-\Delta t$, after numerically moving one state with the teacher solver. Continuous-time consistency takes $\Delta t\to0$. This removes the particular finite interval from the objective, but it does not make numerical issues disappear from computation. The derivative along the teacher path is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}\bm{f}_{\theta^-}}{\mathrm{d}t}=\nabla_{\bm{x}_t}\bm{f}_{\theta^-}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}\bm{x}_t}{\mathrm{d}t}+\partial_t\bm{f}_{\theta^-}.$$

The superscript $\theta^-$ means stop-gradient parameters. The first term is a Jacobian-vector product: it asks how the output changes when the input moves in the teacher velocity direction. The second term measures direct dependence on time.

sections.title: Why continuous mathematics still meets numerical reality
sections.markdown:
It is easy to misread “continuous-time” as “free of approximation.” The claim is narrower: the training objective is obtained from an infinitesimal consistency limit and is not tied to a manually selected adjacent-time spacing. Actual models still evaluate derivatives, use finite precision, and ultimately generate with a finite number of network evaluations.

The Euler figure makes that distinction concrete using the unrelated toy ODE $\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t=-x$, $x(0)=1$. Its exact solution is $x(t)=e^{-t}$, while forward Euler uses $x_{k+1}=x_k-hx_k$ for step size $h$. For an illustrative calculation with $h=0.5$, the first two updates are $x_1=1-0.5=0.5$ and $x_2=0.5-0.25=0.25$; the exact value at $t=1$ is $e^{-1}\approx0.368$, so the absolute error is about $0.118$. Changing $h$ shows how discretization changes a numerical trajectory. This is not the teacher solver, an adaptive integrator, or a learned rCM field; it only separates a continuous equation from its finite computation.

sections.title: Making the tangent computable at scale
sections.markdown:
The original sCM formulation uses the TrigFlow schedule $\alpha_t=\cos t$ and $\sigma_t=\sin t$, but large pretrained teachers may use another schedule. rCM’s implementation constructs a wrapped teacher by choosing a raw teacher time $\phi(t)$ satisfying

$$\frac{\sigma_{\phi(t)}}{\alpha_{\phi(t)}}=\tan t.$$

This matches signal-to-noise ratio. The raw teacher input is rescaled appropriately, and its denoiser output is converted into the TrigFlow velocity parameterization. The paper reports performing these conversions in FP64.

The larger engineering obstacle is the JVP. Standard forward-mode tooling did not directly fit the authors’ sharded setup, so layers accept both ordinary activations and tangent inputs. Their FlashAttention-2 kernel propagates the attention tangent with blockwise tiling. FSDP remains compatible when sharding follows layer boundaries. Under Ulysses context parallelism, both the query-key-value tensors and their tangents undergo the same all-to-all redistribution. These changes concern exact derivative propagation through the deployed architecture; they do not alter the conceptual consistency target.

sections.title: The failure mode: local agreement can drift globally
sections.markdown:
When scaled to text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, pure sCM produced sharp samples but struggled with fine text, stable geometry, and temporal consistency. The paper links this to error accumulation. In its TrigFlow derivative, the teacher discrepancy is weighted by $\cos t$, whereas JVP self-feedback is weighted by $\sin t$. At large $t$, the ratio $\cos t/\sin t$ approaches zero, weakening direct teacher supervision while self-feedback dominates. Small student errors can therefore propagate toward noisier times.

This motivates a second path with a longer reach. Consistency training uses externally supplied clean or teacher-generated states and encourages coverage of their trajectories. Score distillation instead evaluates student-generated, or on-policy, samples and pushes their distribution toward the teacher. The authors describe the former as mode-covering and the latter as mode-seeking. A common misconception is that one objective is universally better. Their roles are complementary: coverage can preserve diversity yet spread probability too broadly, while aggressive mode seeking can sharpen samples yet discard alternatives.

sections.title: rCM adds a long-skip distribution correction
sections.markdown:
The proposed objective is

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{rCM}}(\theta)=\mathcal{L}_{\text{sCM}}(\theta)+\lambda\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}(\theta).$$

$\mathcal{L}_{\text{sCM}}$ is the instantaneous consistency loss, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}$ is the score-based distribution-matching loss, and $\lambda$ is their balancing weight. For a student sample $\bm{x}_0\sim p_\theta$, its noised state $\bm{x}_t$, and $t\sim p_D$, the paper defines

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\bm{x}_0-\operatorname{sg}\!\left[\bm{x}_0-\frac{\bm{f}_{\text{fake}}(\bm{x}_t,t)-\bm{f}_{\text{teacher}}(\bm{x}_t,t)}{\operatorname{mean}(\operatorname{abs}(\bm{x}_0-\bm{f}_{\text{teacher}}(\bm{x}_t,t)))}\right]\right\|_2^2\right].$$

The numerator is the difference between the fake denoiser, which proxies the intractable score of the few-step student distribution, and the fixed teacher denoiser. The denominator normalizes that signal by the mean absolute teacher denoising error for the sample. The expression inside $\operatorname{sg}[\cdot]$ is treated as a fixed target: differentiating the squared loss therefore updates the student-generated $\bm{x}_0$ toward that target, yielding an update direction determined by the normalized fake-versus-teacher denoiser difference without backpropagating through the target construction.

For each rollout, the number of simulation steps $N$ is sampled between $1$ and $N_{\max}$. Candidate times are drawn stochastically and clipped to create a nonincreasing sequence. Reverse denoising alternates with forward noising, but DMD gradients pass only through the last denoising transition. Thus the regularizer observes outcomes reached across long skips without backpropagating through the whole rollout.

Training alternates two distinct updates. The student is optimized with the combined rCM objective above. Separately, the fake network is refreshed on current student-generated samples using the flow-matching target

$$\mathcal{L}(\theta_{\text{fake}})=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x}_0\sim p_\theta,\bm{\epsilon},t\sim p_D}\left[\left\|\bm{F}_{\text{fake}}(\bm{x}_t,t)-\bm{v}\right\|_2^2\right],$$

where $\bm{v}$ is the diffusion velocity target. This alternating update keeps the auxiliary network aligned with the evolving student distribution so that it remains a usable proxy for the otherwise intractable student score.

The paper also treats derivative stability as scale-dependent: a finite-difference approximation to the explicit time derivative was stable for 2B-scale image models, whereas 10B-plus models and video used a full JVP with FP32 time-embedding layers.

sections.title: What the reported numbers establish—and what they do not
sections.markdown:
The evidence spans Cosmos-Predict2 image models from 0.6B to 14B parameters and Wan2.1 video models at 1.3B and 14B. On GenEval at $1360\times768$, the 14B Cosmos rCM scored $0.83$ with four function evaluations. On VBench for $832\times480\times81$ video, the 14B Wan rCM scored $85.05$ with two evaluations and reached $8.3$ FPS under batch size one on a single H100, with sampling and VAE decoding included.

Those results are conditional, not universal speed or quality constants. Metrics, resolution, hardware, decoding cost, prompts, and model family matter. The authors explicitly caution that surpassing a teacher’s aggregate VBench score does not prove superiority in diversity or physical consistency. They also report that one-step video remained blurry, while two steps approached teacher scores and four steps improved details.

The $\lambda$ ablation sharpens the central trade-off. For Wan2.1 1.3B trained for 10,000 iterations at batch size 64, larger $\lambda$ improved quality but reduced diversity; smaller $\lambda$ reversed that tendency. At the tested order-of-magnitude grid, $0.01$ was the smallest value preserving good quality. This is evidence for that experimental family, not a theorem that $0.01$ is optimal for every dataset, architecture, or budget. rCM’s contribution is therefore best read as a coupled training principle plus infrastructure, supported across the reported large image and video settings—not as elimination of the quality-diversity trade-off.

quiz.question: Suppose the consistency loss is retained but the DMD weight is set to zero. Which training signal disappears?

options.text: On-policy distribution correction from student-generated samples.
options.explanation: Correct. Setting $\lambda=0$ removes $\mathcal{L}_{\text{DMD}}$, including its student-sample distribution-matching signal.

options.text: The identity boundary condition at time zero.
options.explanation: Incorrect. That boundary belongs to the consistency-function parameterization, not the DMD term.

options.text: The teacher-trajectory tangent used by sCM.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The sCM loss remains and still uses the trajectory derivative and JVP.

quiz.question: Under the paper’s interpretation, why can adding reverse-divergence score distillation help pure sCM?

options.text: It replaces every JVP with an exact closed-form solution.
options.explanation: Incorrect. rCM still requires JVP computation and introduces stabilization strategies for it.

options.text: It adds a long-skip, on-policy signal that can counter accumulated consistency errors.
options.explanation: Correct. The score path evaluates student-generated samples and complements local consistency supervision.

options.text: It guarantees that every teacher mode receives equal student probability.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Reverse divergence is described as mode-seeking and can reduce diversity when weighted too strongly.

quiz.question: A distilled video model has a higher aggregate VBench score than its teacher. What is the warranted conclusion?

options.text: It is superior to the teacher on every aspect of video generation.
options.explanation: Incorrect. An aggregate score does not establish better diversity, physical consistency, or every component metric.

options.text: The teacher is unnecessary for training future students.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The reported method still uses the teacher denoiser and teacher trajectory supervision.

options.text: It scored higher under that evaluation, but broader superiority is not established.
options.explanation: Correct. The conclusion must remain tied to the stated benchmark and evaluation conditions.
